laneTitle: P-98b: one billing-interval vocabulary, month/year, end to end
status: complete -- both halves built, both suites green, gate verified by violation. Diffs are UNCOMMITTED in two worktrees, per the dispatch commit clause.
missionPremise: Operator ruling carried in the compiled dispatch (Nick, 2026-08-31): ONE billing-interval vocabulary end to end -- 'month' / 'year', Stripe's own recurring-interval grammar -- with no translation layer, and the client changed to match rather than the server. The rationale in the dispatch is that a silent mapping between two vocabularies for one subject is the defect class that already cost this operation a re-stamp of 6.3M rows when a legacy access-policy pair had to be removed. The source authority is lib/db/drizzle/0092_pe_billing_interval.sql, whose CHECK admits only NULL, 'month' and 'year', and whose comment states the grammar mirrors Stripe.
completionPredicate: peWireBillingInterval.ts no longer exists in the tree; no billing-interval VALUE in either repo's entitlement path is 'monthly' or 'annual' except as a deliberately-refused input in a violation test; the three assertions that failed CI pass WITHOUT being edited; npx tsc --noEmit is clean in both repos; the client suite is at or above its pre-change count; and the annual_upgrade gate has been observed RED under a deliberate inversion and green again after restore, with the red output captured verbatim. All met.
scopeBasis: The subject is the entitlement WIRE FIELD pe_user_entitlements.billing_interval and every reader of it. Display copy and UI toggle state are out of scope: they are not a wire vocabulary and already sit behind a declared, tested boundary (pricing.ts toCheckoutInterval). Persisted identifiers containing the substring 'annual' -- the annual_upgrade rung id -- are out of scope because they name a rung, not an interval, and renaming one to satisfy a text match would break a stored vocabulary.

LESSON: grep -c $'\r' is VACUOUS in this environment: the escape does not survive into the pattern, grep gets an empty pattern, and it reports every line as matching. It returned '269 CR lines' for a file with zero CR bytes. Use cr=$(tr -cd '\r' < f | wc -c). Negative control that proves it: printf 'a\nb\n' > f; grep -c $'\r' f returns 2. This is the ENFORCEMENT 'convenient answer, uninterrogated instrument' shape, caught only because od -c disagreed.

Both property-seat worktrees are checked out LF-ONLY in the working tree even though core.autocrlf=true. Rewriting a file with python io.open(..., newline='') therefore matches the checkout and produces a clean semantic diff. Writing CRLF would produce a whole-file diff.

To measure a real BEFORE count without a second checkout: back the diff up, git stash push (path-scoped where possible), run the suite, git stash pop, then regenerate the diff and compare md5 to the backup. The md5 match is the proof the restore was byte-identical, and it costs one command. This worked on both repos here.

A package's `test` script is not always `vitest run`. apps/property-explorer runs `node scripts/pe-chrome-kit-gate.mjs && vitest run`, so a bare vitest run skips a real gate. Read the script before claiming a suite is green.

When a translation module is deleted, the strongest single check that no importer was orphaned is a clean `tsc --noEmit` over the whole project -- stronger than grepping for the symbol, because it follows re-exports.
DEAD-END: Do not try to establish a baseline by `git checkout -- <files>` in a lane worktree: it is refused as destructive, and correctly so. git stash push / pop is the sanctioned path and is reversible with a provable restore.

Do not anchor a multi-line patch on remembered indentation. A doc-comment anchor with 3 leading spaces instead of 1 failed to match and aborted the patch script -- which is the right failure, because the script asserts an exact occurrence count of 1 before writing. Anchor patches on text read from the file in the same session.
